If we post fresh content, nobody even sees it in the subverse unless they remember to sort by new. To all appearances, nothing has been added since last their visit if they don't.

I propose we position new posts at the top of the list so they at least get seen by subscribers. If it gets downvoted it will fall, but at least it will be seen.

Thanks for reading.

As calories are the easiest way to get the body to use up excess fat deposits, an option is intermittent fasting, which involves cutting down calorie intake during fasting periods, and then going into normal eating mode when not fasting. There are many variations of this fasting, and there are many long term benefits of putting your body into 'survival mode'.

This is just one example: The 5:2 Diet

Should you endeavour on this fasting journey, you might want to incorporate eating habits from the Okinawan people on your normal eating days, such as not completely eating until you are full (stop at around 80-90%). This keeps the body in the 'survival mode' by signalling that there is a shortage of food.

I'll just correct you - when doing intermittent fasting, you actually want to avoid your body going to "starvation response" (official medical term) which actually causes your metabolism to slow down. The whole purpose of intermittent fasting is to have a few days of starvation here and there while your body is working in regular or heightened metabolism state (which should happen with 5:2).

Not starvation. I'll clear that up in a minute. Intermittent fasting does have viability with some people. Starvation isn't the right word here. IF works on a continued burn for short periods of time. OP used "survival" not starvation. I'm not well versed enough with what all goes on with IF to know if that's the right terminology but I have done enough poking around what starvation mode is to know that IF isn't it.

Clarification: This is NOT entering starvation mode. Starvation mode/response kicks in only after your glycogen reserves are depleted and after the 2-3 days of fatty acid burn. Intermittent fasting (IF) works by taking advantage of the 2-3 day fatty acid burn. Yes, it also burns muscle.

To explain it, you eat normally for five days and eat at rediculusly low levels for two. Hence, IF 5:2. The five days allow you to build up a glycemic index again so you don't reduce your metabolism. The formula does work in general, but if you decide to pig out on your five days of regular eating you're gonna have a bad time. I guess what's being called "the Okinawan method" satisfies this, but if you know what your Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) is on an average day you can eat at or below maintenance with no issue.

NOTE: If this method works for you then that's fantastic. If it doesn't then don't quit trying until you find your thing.
